basic_identification.full_title: Structural Steel — Part 2 Hot Rolled Quenched and Tempered Steel Plates, Sheets, Strips and Wide Flats
basic_identification.sector_category: Metallurgical Engineering (finalised by the Wrought Steel Products Sectional Committee) [1]

scope.summary: This standard specifies requirements for hot-rolled quenched and tempered steel plates, sheets, strips, and wide flats for structural purposes. It covers high-strength structural steel grades divided into S grades and SG grades designed for demanding engineering or structural loads.

version_status_and_amendments.supersedes: IS 2062 : 2011 (partially superseded as structural steel standards are split into multiple parts)
version_status_and_amendments.amendment_slips: No amendments found (newly established standard in 2026) [1].

certification_and_marking.standard_type: Product Specification (High-Strength Structural Steel Plates / Sheets)
certification_and_marking.certification_status: Strict Statutory Mandatory Certification. Under the 'Steel and Steel Products (Quality Control) Order' issued by the Ministry of Steel, Government of India, all structural steel products sold, stocked, or imported in India must carry the mandatory BIS Standard Mark (ISI Mark). Export-only products conform to buyer specifications but are exempt. Precious metal hallmarking is completely inapplicable to heavy structural steel products, as it is reserved strictly for gold and silver jewelry under national BIS frameworks.

requirements.detail: Every conforming structural steel plate, sheet, or strip must bear the BIS Standard Mark (ISI Mark) stamped or embossed permanently on a visible face.

Heat analysis for SG grades must strictly satisfy maximum limits for Carbon (0.18% to 0.22%), Manganese (1.70% to 2.00%), Sulphur (0.035% to 0.040%), Phosphorus (0.035%), and other alloying elements like Silicon, Nickel, Chromium, Molybdenum, and Boron [3].

To ensure excellent site weldability, maximum carbon equivalent (CE) limits based on ladle analysis are restricted depending on grade, quality, and nominal thickness. For example, grade ISH S460Q (Qualities C, D, E) must not exceed 0.47% for thickness <= 50 mm, or 0.48% for thickness > 50 mm to 100 mm [4].

When specified at the time of order, product analysis must be carried out on the finished structural product. Permissible variations between product analysis and ladle analysis are strictly limited per Table 3 (for S grades) and Table 4 (for SG grades) [5].

High-toughness S grades must satisfy strict minimum transverse Charpy V-notch energy absorption values at sub-zero temperatures: Quality C is tested at 0 °C (Min 30 J to 40 J), Quality D is tested at -20 °C (Min 27 J to 35 J), and Quality E is tested at -40 °C or -60 °C (Min 27 J to 40 J) depending on the grade [6]. For thicknesses <= 12 mm using sub-sized test pieces, the energy limits are reduced proportionally to the cross-sectional area [7].

plain_language_summary.summary: IS 2062 (Part 2) : 2026 is the strict national Indian Standard safety specification governing hot-rolled quenched and tempered steel plates, sheets, strips, and wide flats utilized in demanding structural and civil engineering projects [5]. In accordance with India's national Steel Quality Control Order, all structural steel supplied to the domestic market must carry the mandatory BIS Standard Mark (ISI Mark). This second part of the standard establishes strict mechanical and chemical limits—including maximum carbon equivalent (CE) limits to ensure reliable site welding [4], product analysis variation tolerances [5], and sub-zero Charpy V-notch impact toughness requirements down to -60 °C [6]—to prevent sudden brittle fractures in critical high-stress structural joints.
